payload.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

ambiguities: Whether 'maximal' means global maximum over all real x (most likely) or maximal element in some other restricted class of x (not specified).
Whether the question asks for a unique x, a set of x, or a description of all x achieving the maximum (wording suggests determining the argmax set).
Dependence on n is not explicitly stated: the maximum value is presumably a function of n, but the question does not specify whether the answer should be expressed in terms of n.
implicit_assumptions_surfaced: The phrase 'maximal' is intended to mean global maximum over all real x, not merely a local maximum.
It is assumed the expression has a finite maximum value over the entire set of real numbers (that max exists rather than only a supremum).
The floor function behavior on real inputs is assumed to be standard: floor(t) is the greatest integer less than or equal to t.

domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n is greater than 1
k is an integer satisfying 1 <= k <= n (so the sum is over n terms)
floor is applied to real numbers and returns an integer
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Fix an integer n greater than 1. Let f_n(x) = floor(n times x) minus the sum for integer k from 1 to n of floor(k times x) divided by k. Consider f_n as a function on all real numbers x. Determine all real x values at which f_n(x) is globally maximal, and determine the corresponding maximal value M(n) = max over real x of f_n(x).
quantifier_order: For a fixed integer n with n > 1
For real x (x ranges over all real numbers)
Choose x that achieves the maximum of the given expression over all real x

variables.name: n
variables.role: fixed parameter of the optimization problem; also upper limit of the sum

variables.name: x
variables.role: decision variable over which the expression is maximized

variables.name: k
variables.role: dummy index in the finite sum, constrained by 1 <= k <= n

variables.name: M
variables.role: the maximal value of the expression as a function of n

witness_dependencies: An optimal x (or the set of optimal x values) may depend on n
The maximal value M may depend on n
